subject: conditioning upon being connected to the internet

messages.author: b949e0841d7e094b
messages.subject: conditioning upon being connected to the internet
parts:
Dear all,

I just noticed that gvisTable from the googleVis package requires an internet connection to work properly. This is not a problem when the app is hosted on its server, but becomes a problem when I use it offline. Since it would be tedious to have two versions of the app, I'd like to wrap the gvisTable command around a conditional, like say:

if (internetConnection == True) {gvisTable(blabla)}
else something_else

Any suggestions?

many thanks,

Patrick.

messages.subject: Re: conditioning upon being connected to the internet
parts:
I tried to use the getURL() function of the RCurl package.

In ui.R, I had a tabPanel with:

      tabPanel(
        h2("Test")
        , suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(
            if (is.character(getURL("www.google.com")))
              {htmlOutput("tableOnline")}
            else {htmlOutput("tableOffline")}
          ))
        , value = 1
      )

where in server.R I have

output$tableOffline <- renderTable({print(blabla)})
output$tableOnline <- renderGvis({gvisTable(blabla)})
 
but while it works when I'm online, it fails when I'm offline with the following error message:

ERROR: Could not resolve host: www.google.com; nodename nor servname provided, or not known

So clearly suppressMessages(suppressWarnings( blabla )) is not helping here.

Has anyone done something like this?

suggestions welcome,

thanks!

messages.subject: Re: conditioning upon being connected to the internet
parts:
The question arose because I was trying to use the googleVis package to display pretty tables but googleVis will work only online, so I was looking for a way to use googleVis only when connected to the internet. 

In the meantime, I have got rid of googleVis altogether and defined styles that make my table look reasonably good without googleVis.

The following produces alternately-colored rows, removes vertical lines and sets a horizontal border in the same color as the even-colored background just in case. Also added padding to air the table. What's missing from the googleVis capabilities is pageing, but I'll live with it in the meantime. 

    tags$head(
      tags$style(type='text/css'
          , ".data tr:nth-child(even){background-color: rgb(245,245,245);}" # even-numbered rows background
          , ".table-bordered td, .table-bordered th {border-top: 1px solid rgb(245,245,245);}" # horizontal lines
          , ".table-bordered {border-width: 0px;}" # suppress border around whole table
          , ".table-bordered td, .table-bordered th {border-left: none;}" # suppress vertical lines
          , ".table-condensed td, .table-condensed th {padding: 5px 20px;}" # pad vertical/horizontal
      )
    )

Thanks Stéphane.

parts:
First use try() with option silent=TRUE. Then look at the class of the result. If there's an error then the class is try-error.

> trying <- try(2+2, silent=TRUE)
> str(trying)
 num 4
> class(trying)
[1] "numeric"
> trying <- try(2+"a", silent=TRUE)
> str(trying)
Class 'try-error'  atomic [1:1] Error in 2 + "a" : non-numeric argument to binary operator

  ..- attr(*, "condition")=List of 2
  .. ..$ message: chr "non-numeric argument to binary operator"
  .. ..$ call   : language 2 + "a"
  .. ..- attr(*, "class")= chr [1:3] "simpleError" "error" "condition"
> class(trying)
[1] "try-error"

That was silly of me...

The only problem is that this will catch any kind of error, not just not managing to get online, for instance if I forget to load the package RCurl. So it's something to bear in mind with the following.

try(getURL("www.google.com"),'silent'=FALSE)
Error in try(getURL("www.google.com"), silent = FALSE) :

library("RCurl")
if(class(try(getURL("www.google.com"),'silent'=TRUE))=="try-error"){print("try-error caught")}else{print("Online, probably")}
